I read the whole clause and the signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers the recitals and every operative sentence; nothing outside it is a command (any attached lists of carriers or unions identify parties and are not commands). The one operative clause creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. 160, to investigate the dispute involving the Southern Pacific Company (Pacific Lines) and certain of its employees; it bars board members from pecuniary or other interest in any carrier or employee organization; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and it recites the statutory standstill: from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change except by agreement is to be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled \"Revocation of Various Executive Orders\", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and \"any amendments thereto, are revoked:\" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: \"11042 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute\". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The quoted source for the end is the enacting paragraph of EO 12553, which names no order; the order is named by its row in the No./Subject table, quoted above, so the table row and the enacting paragraph are read together. The thirty-day report deadline and the standstill that runs to thirty days after the report are periods measured by the order's own terms. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, neither the report nor the end of the standstill ends the order; each is a spent fact, and the order stayed on the books until it was expressly revoked. The order was functionally spent once the board had reported and the standstill had run, but this claim assigns no date to that point because no report date is cited from a registered source here; a board report held as a lead-grade Government printing is not cited, and a dated transmittal letter is not proof of receipt or of standstill expiry. Earlier candidates: a search of the held order texts for citations of this order by number found no later order that revokes, amends or extends it; the Office of the Federal Register catalog notes name EO 12553 as the revoking order. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception, and the order created no continuing right or obligation outside its own terms.   Exact retained record text (unshared):
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the carrier, or by its employees, in the conditions out of which these disputes arose.

Kennedy) dated 1962-09-14; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Creating an emergency board to investigate disputes between the REA Express and certain of its employees). I read the whole clause and the signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers the recitals and every operative sentence; nothing outside it is a command (any attached lists of carriers or unions identify parties and are not commands). The one operative clause creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. 160, to investigate the dispute involving the REA Express and certain of its employees; it bars board members from pecuniary or other interest in any carrier or employee organization; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and it recites the statutory standstill: from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change except by agreement is to be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled \"Revocation of Various Executive Orders\", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and \"any amendments thereto, are revoked:\" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: \"11050 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes\". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The quoted source for the end is the enacting paragraph of EO 12553, which names no order; the order is named by its row in the No./Subject table, quoted above, so the table row and the enacting paragraph are read together. The thirty-day report deadline and the standstill that runs to thirty days after the report are periods measured by the order's own terms. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, neither the report nor the end of the standstill ends the order; each is a spent fact, and the order stayed on the books until it was expressly revoked. The order was functionally spent once the board had reported and the standstill had run, but this claim assigns no date to that point because no report date is cited from a registered source here; a board report held as a lead-grade Government printing is not cited, and a dated transmittal letter is not proof of receipt or of standstill expiry. Earlier candidates: a search of the held order texts for citations of this order by number found no later order that revokes, amends or extends it; the Office of the Federal Register catalog notes name EO 12553 as the revoking order. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception, and the order created no continuing right or obligation outside its own terms. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Own-terms periods (report deadline and standstill) are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21. Later orders that merely recite or list this order would not be ends; none was found that does more than EO 12553.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"The order has no command independent of the board: the standstill is recited from the statute and depends on the board's creation and report. No other command in the order, and no other order that incorporates it, was found in the held texts.\",\"savings_check\":\"EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception (searched as described); the board's report and any settlement or later legislation are not obligations created by this order and are not claimed as surviving effects.\",\"scope_check\":\"Single clause, whole order. As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by The Pullman Company, the Chicago, Rock Island & Pacific Railroad Company, the New York Central System and The Soo Line Railroad Company, or by its employees, in the conditions out of which this dispute arose.

I read the whole clause and the signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers the recitals and every operative sentence; nothing outside it is a command (any attached lists of carriers or unions identify parties and are not commands). The one operative clause creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. 160, to investigate the dispute involving United Air Lines, Inc., and certain of its employees; it bars board members from pecuniary or other interest in any carrier or employee organization; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and it recites the statutory standstill: from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change except by agreement is to be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled \"Revocation of Various Executive Orders\", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and \"any amendments thereto, are revoked:\" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: \"11121 Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute\". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The quoted source for the end is the enacting paragraph of EO 12553, which names no order; the order is named by its row in the No./Subject table, quoted above, so the table row and the enacting paragraph are read together. The thirty-day report deadline and the standstill that runs to thirty days after the report are periods measured by the order's own terms. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, neither the report nor the end of the standstill ends the order; each is a spent fact, and the order stayed on the books until it was expressly revoked. The order was functionally spent once the board had reported and the standstill had run, but this claim assigns no date to that point because no report date is cited from a registered source here; a board report held as a lead-grade Government printing is not cited, and a dated transmittal letter is not proof of receipt or of standstill expiry. Earlier candidates: a search of the held order texts for citations of this order by number found no later order that revokes, amends or extends it; the Office of the Federal Register catalog notes name EO 12553 as the revoking order. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception, and the order created no continuing right or obligation outside its own terms. Kennedy) dated 1963-11-09; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Creating an emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Florida East Coast Railway Company and certain of its employees). I read the whole clause and the signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers the recitals and every operative sentence; nothing outside it is a command (any attached lists of carriers or unions identify parties and are not commands). The one operative clause creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. 160, to investigate the dispute involving the Florida East Coast Railway Company and certain of its employees; it bars board members from pecuniary or other interest in any carrier or employee organization; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and it recites the statutory standstill: from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change except by agreement is to be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled \"Revocation of Various Executive Orders\", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and \"any amendments thereto, are revoked:\" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: \"11127 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute\". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The packet holds no located acting-provision record for this pair (the dossier lists the target provision as not located), so the end is cited to the complete held text of EO 12553 (Federal Register copy, 51 FR 7237), which contains both the enacting paragraph and the table row quoted above; I read the whole text and the row is present on its own line. The thirty-day report deadline and the standstill that runs to thirty days after the report are periods measured by the order's own terms. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, neither the report nor the end of the standstill ends the order; each is a spent fact, and the order stayed on the books until it was expressly revoked. The order was functionally spent once the board had reported and the standstill had run, but this claim assigns no date to that point because no report date is cited from a registered source here; a board report held as a lead-grade Government printing is not cited, and a dated transmittal letter is not proof of receipt or of standstill expiry. Earlier candidates: a search of the held order texts for citations of this order by number found no later order that revokes, amends or extends it; the Office of the Federal Register catalog notes name EO 12553 as the revoking order. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception, and the order created no continuing right or obligation outside its own terms. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Own-terms periods (report deadline and standstill) are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21. No held source shows an earlier revocation, supersession, expiry or termination. The first ending shown by held evidence is the express revocation by number in EO 12553, effective 1986-02-25. Later orders that merely recite or list this order would not be ends; none was found that does more than EO 12553.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"The order has no command independent of the board: the standstill is recited from the statute and depends on the board's creation and report. No other command in the order, and no other order that incorporates it, was found in the held texts.\",\"savings_check\":\"EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception (searched as described); the board's report and any settlement or later legislation are not obligations created by this order and are not claimed as surviving effects.\",\"scope_check\":\"Single clause, whole order. As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the above named air carriers or by their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

Status provisional NO, unchanged. The order creates a three-member board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the disputes between the carriers represented by the Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees (List A) and employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen ('I hereby create; a board of three members', offset 1559 onward), directs it to report 'within thirty days from the date o f this order' (offset 1798 onward) and recites the section 10 status quo (offset 2075 onward). The carrier list (List A) after the signature is an attached schedule identifying the parties, not a separate command. Deciding source: EO 12553 of 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237, jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt), whose operative sentence (offsets 691-966) revokes 'the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto', and whose table names this order ('11135 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes', offsets 19627-19699); no effective-date wording, so effective on signing 1986-02-25. The dossier lists 'target provision not located: EO:12553' because the machine scanner found no ACT record; I located the naming entry myself ('11135 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes' at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt offsets 19627-19699, inside the table introduced by the operative sentence at 691-966), so the end cites the held EO 12553 text as a whole (ACTOR_TEXT) with those offsets named here. Report-deadline ruling (2026-10-21, option C) applied: the report deadline (1964-02-02 (signing date 1964-01-03 plus 30 days; counting convention not ruled)) and the report itself are spent facts, not ends. The board's actual report (its date, and so the end of the 30-day status quo) is not held in the repository (no NMB report text under jobs/source-ladder/output/texts; no FETCH_QUEUE line yet), so the 'functionally spent' date is disclosed as unknown; under the report-deadline ruling it is not an end and does not change the first end. D6 / later events: the dossier chain and actor provisions show only EO 12553; the draft's later-event and whole-order-end proposals (OFR disposition note 'Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986' and the 1989 Codification table 'Revoked by EO 12553') point to the same instrument and are attached as the end itself; a by-number scan of all held FR order texts and APP texts found no other naming instrument (EO_10298 and EO_10299 (16 FR 11135 page number), EO_11912 (FR Doc. 76-11135), EO_12553 (the revocation)).
